factual_methodology.summary: Verified Japanese 23 Oct official September 2025-base CPI headline and two exclusions; Eurostat 21 Oct Q2 EA21 debt levels, annual EA20/EA21 membership distinctions and composition; Freddie Mac 22 Oct 7.32 and 6.68 offered fixed rates; NAR Sept pending-sales contraction; Sep BCB rate and IMF October risk framework. Report distinguishes time references, concepts and conditional inference.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Distinct from Oct 22 labor/energy inventory issue and Oct 21 UK sovereign debt; new Japan CPI and US mortgage rate interact with EA21 debt and global refinancing. Financial/real evidence and falsifiers are explicit.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three parallel quantitative bar charts in both locales (CPI 2.1, 2.1, 2.4; euro government debt 88.8, 82.9, 63.4, 119.1, 139.9; 30-year mortgages 7.40, 7.32), substantive comparable tables, one flow, one qualitative regional map. Numeric parity checked.

research_depth.summary: Over 2,400 words EN and 2,700 PT with six substantive sections, unit and membership restrictions, financing mechanisms, alternative explanations, global spillovers, falsifiers and observation agenda.

evidence_traceability.summary: Nine identical URLs across Japan Statistics Bureau, Eurostat Q2 and annual, Freddie Mac survey and archive, NAR, IMF October GFSR/WEO and BCB September Copom. Highlighted output and mortgage facts supported by dated original institutional publications.

counterfactual_review.summary: Contrasts persistent imported-price pressure vs transient CPI factors, refinancing shock vs long existing-maturity insulation, rates vs housing inventory as drivers of contracts, and financial repricing conditional on observable actual flows and margins.

contrary_evidence: September CPI is a one-month observation; a higher exclusion-based rate is not a wage-price causal estimate.
Debt/GDP can rise from denominator effects and fall with nominal GDP gains without an equal movement in nominal debt; quarterly EA21 and annual EA20 memberships differ.
September pending US contracts precede the 22 Oct weekly rate easing; inventory availability and credit approval can matter separately.
A Japanese price release alone does not establish official monetary tightening or yen-funded cross-border liquidation.
limitations: Internal sourced bilingual QA verifies selected institutional anchors and calculations, not external peer review or an independently audited asset-allocation exposure study.
Observed early Friday Oct 23 Japan inflation is included; releases scheduled for later in the European and American trading day are excluded.
Illustrative US 30-year annuity assumes constant principal, 360 fixed payments and excludes fees, insurance and down payment.
notes: Editorial integrity check against original public statistics, semantic and numeric EN/PT comparison; correction of illustrative payment made before QA; no unpublished central-bank decisions or invented market yields.
